notes: clipping_of is a subproperty of derived_from, which is transitive (RELATIONS.md). The source words' own etymologies (business < busy, omnibus < omnis) and minibus < bus are firm background facts the record states as bridges (omnibus < omnis, which the original answer of q1 needs, since 2026-10-31).

queries.not_checked: fol: compares strings (which end of the source word the clipping kept)

fol.notes: clipping_of (RELATIONS.md) over a Word enum; kept_part (ATTRIBUTES.md) is read off whether the source word's spelling (a string literal paired with each candidate in a finite quantifier) begins or ends with 'bus' (firm definition). Spellings as literals, not a string function: a free spelling made core minimisation time out.

kept_rule.says: A clipping keeps the beginning of its source word if the source ('omnibus', 'business') begins with 'bus', else the end if it ends with 'bus'.
kept_rule.z3: All([w, sp], [(omnibus, 'omnibus'), (business, 'business')], Implies(clipping_of(bus, w), If(startswith(sp, 'bus'), kept_part(bus) == beginning, Implies(endswith(sp, 'bus'), kept_part(bus) == end))))

label_corrections.why: With the source words' spellings as firm per-word facts (omnibus : EndsWithBus, business : BeginsWithBus), the kept part is a role chain clipping_of then a class membership: DL. The string test only computes those firm facts.
